authority: T0 CP1a kinematic/static common-parent compatibility certificate; not full CP1, a TECT action, a claim-tier change, or a physical-model selection
statement: At every fixed finite Fourier cutoff on the periodic three-torus of side pi/2, one fitted real-scalar local-quartic Hamiltonian family has a common CCR algebra, field, volume, boundary, hbar, regulator, state-selection rule, and relative-energy subtraction. Its r=0 quadratic transverse-constant three-mode subspace has squared frequencies 9,25,25, matching the finite PA-H1 calibration. Its cubic-SOS spatial symbol has exactly the eight lattice zeros (+/-4,+/-4,+/-4), exact off-node lattice gap nine, and node Hessian spectrum 3/2,63/4,63/4. For -9<=r<0 every finite-regulator classical global minimizer has a nonzero node component, and stationary points obey the registered amplitude and off-node concentration bounds. The two roles are coupled by the local quartic. The same construction proves that exact PA-H1 matching occurs only at r=0, the old pure Gaussian state is not the interacting parent ground state, the node cone is anisotropic, and the ultraviolet group speed is unbounded. Therefore this is a structural CP1a benchmark, not full CP1 or a selected physical equation.
verdict: ADVANCE AS A CP1A STRUCTURAL COMPATIBILITY BENCHMARK ONLY; DO NOT SELECT AS THE PHYSICAL EQUATION

No new general theorem is claimed. The repository-specific contribution is the exact convention-level CP1a construction, its simultaneous calibration/ordering compatibility audit, common relative-energy ledger, and explicit rejection criteria.
no_overclaim: This T0 certificate constructs one fitted finite-regulator T3 Hamiltonian family and proves its exact r=0 quadratic PA-H1 calibration, r<0 classical finite-wavevector ordering window, shared relative-energy convention, and exact stated obstructions. It does not derive the old pure Gaussian PA-H1 state from the interacting parent, provide one fixed-r ordered calibration state, prove nonlinear subspace invariance, quantum symmetry breaking, a thermodynamic phase transition, regulator or counterterm removal, an isotropic or causal cone, bounded ultraviolet propagation, a physical vacuum, energy below empty space, cosmic cooling, spacetime, gravity, CP1, CP2, Pre-A, T-050, or Sector A.
